articles.title: Troy Aikman, Joe Buck reportedly got into argument in 'Monday Night Football' booth over contract extension tensions at ESPN
articles.summary: Joe Buck has signed a $100 million extension with ESPN, but Troy Aikman still has not.
articles.body:
Tensions are apparently running high inside the "Monday Night Football" booth.

Longtime broadcaster Joe Buck and Hall of Fame quarterback Troy Aikman got into an argument inside the announcer booth at SoFi Stadium ahead of Monday night's game between the Los Angeles Rams and Buffalo Bills, according to Front Office Sports' Ryan Glasspiegel .

Buck and Aikman's relationship has reportedly been strained ever since Buck reportedly reached a new contract with ESPN last month that is reportedly worth more than $100 million over the next six seasons. The new deal will ensure that Buck will call the Super Bowl both this year and again when ESPN/ABC gets the rights to it in 2031.

Aikman, however, has not received a formal offer on a new deal.

So on Monday night, according to Glasspiegel, Buck "broke the ice" on the unspoken tension between the two. That led to an argument, which eventually de-escalated before the game started. The game carried on normally, and Buck and Aikman called the game without issue.

Aikman spent 12 seasons playing with the Cowboys, and he led the franchise to three Super Bowl titles before he retired after the 2000 campaign. He was inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame in 2006.

Aikman quickly transitioned into broadcasting after his playing career ended, and he joined Buck at Fox in 2002. The pair are the longest-tenured broadcast team in NFL history, and have undoubtedly become among the most recognizable voices in the sport. They left Fox for ESPN in 2022. Aikman reached his contract with ESPN first, and Buck followed weeks later.

It's not known what would happen to Aikman should he split with ESPN after the Super Bowl. While there are several potential landing spots for him at other networks, an NFL world without the Aikman-Buck pairing is one that the sport hasn't seen in decades.

articles.title: Marvin Harrison Jr.'s Status for Texans-Jaguars Revealed, WR's Fantasy Outlook After Cardinals Trade
articles.summary: Wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. is expected to make his Houston Texans debut Sunday against the Jacksonville Jaguars in London, head coach DeMeco Ryans told reporters Wednesday.
articles.body:
Wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. is expected to make his Houston Texans debut Sunday against the Jacksonville Jaguars in London, head coach DeMeco Ryans told reporters Wednesday.

The Texans sent a package including a 2027 second-round pick to the Arizona Cardinals in order to acquire Harrison from the Cardinals on Monday.

Ryans said he expects Harrison to play Sunday but see somewhat limited usage during the Week 6 matchup.

"When you get a player come in late, like Marvin has, it's just, again, what is he able to pick up on?" Ryans said Wednesday. "We'll go through the entire playbook. We'll have set plays, and we'll make sure it's as easy as possible for him to get lined up so he can play fast.

"Don't expect him to come out and play all 60 snaps in a game, but we'll make sure he gets what he needs, and make sure he's confident in what we're asking him to do."

Harrison has experience playing with Texans quarterback C.J. Stroud from their overlapping time at Ohio State.

That could potentially help Harrison eventually make his case for an increase over his workload in Arizona, where Cardinals quarterback Jacoby Brissett targeted him just 13 times for five catches in four games this season.

Harrison was listed as inactive for the Cardinals' Week 5 matchup before he was traded Monday. He joined Stroud and the Texans for his first team practice Wednesday.

Ryans expressed hope Harrison would be able to quickly adjust to the Texans system after beginning work on the playbook the night he arrived in Houston.

"Getting a player caught up, it isn't hard when the player is attentive and he's locked in on getting the details down... I'm excited to see how his week continues to progress, and see how much he can handle," Ryans said.

Stroud has been leaning this season on Nico Collins, who despite missing two games leads the Texans with 249 receiving yards.

Ryans said he is "excited" to see Harrison and Collins play together in part because he feels both receivers for contested catches.

Harrison is listed as backup to Collins on the Texans' unofficial depth chart. Should Harrison establish himself as a WR2, he could potentially take snaps away from Xavier Hutchinson and Kayshon Boutte, while Jaylin Noel could continue serving as the Texans' slot receiver going forward.

It could take some time for Harrison to establish himself as the Texans' second option behind Collins.

Even in the short term, however, the limited usage Harrison saw as a Cardinal and the Texans' pass-first offense could mean the third-year wide receiver will see a boost in usage as soon as Sunday's game in London.

articles.title: C.J. Stroud Praises Marvin Harrison Jr., Says 'Special' WR Will Be 'Great' for Texans After Trade
articles.summary: Houston Texans quarterback C.J. Stroud has been impressed with Marvin Harrison Jr. after the team recently acquired the wide receiver in a trade with the Arizona Cardinals.
articles.body:
Houston Texans quarterback C.J. Stroud has been impressed with Marvin Harrison Jr. after the team recently acquired the wide receiver in a trade with the Arizona Cardinals.

"I've always thought he was special," Stroud said Wednesday, per Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston. "His work ethic, it's the same thing now"

He also detailed how they work together on the field.

"Runs great routes, very quarterback friendly receiver," Stroud explained, per Wilson . "I'm a pocket quarterback who likes to throw it to him on time. That's when he's at his best."

Stroud and Harrison are already familiar with playing alongside each other, previously spending time together at Ohio State from 2021-22.

Stroud also envisioned Harrison as a strong fit in a receiving corps that includes Nico Collins, Kayshon Boutte, Xavier Hutchinson and Jaylin Noel.

"He'll fit in fine," Stroud said regarding Harrison, per Wilson . "He'll be great for us."

Houston added Harrison and a 2027 sixth-round draft pick from Arizona in exchange for a 2027 second-round pick and a seventh-round pick on Sunday.

Expectations were high for Harrison after the Cardinals selected him with the No. 4 overall pick in the 2024 NFL draft.

While he started off slow as a rookie, he still finished his inaugural season with 62 catches for 885 yards and eight touchdowns.

Harrison took a step back the following year, hauling in 41 receptions for 608 yards and four scores. It's worth noting that he missed five games due to injuries .

Still, Harrison wasn't able to establish himself as a threat in Arizona's passing attack to begin this season. In four appearances, he caught just five passes for 85 yards and one touchdown.

The 24-year-old will look to get his career back on track following the change of scenery.

Houston has dealt with several injuries to its wide receivers in 2026, as Jayden Higgins suffered a torn ACL in training camp while Tank Dell has yet to make his season debut as he recovers from a knee injury .

The Texans own a mere 1-4 record, although they're looking to turn their season around and clinch a fourth consecutive playoff berth. Houston started 0-3 in 2025, but still finished at 12-5 and advanced to the postseason.

Stroud has been efficient to open his 2026 campaign despite Houston's overall struggles, completing 64.3 percent of his throws for 1,402 yards and six touchdowns without getting picked off.

articles.title: Carolina Panthers lineman Taylor Moton overcame bloody, life-threatening episode and now he's back at practice
articles.summary: Taylor Moton describes coughing up blood and the terrifying discovery of multiple clots in his right lung that put his life at serious risk.
articles.body: This is a comeback story of the highest order because Taylor Moton's life was at risk, blood was splattered all over his chest, and doctors frantically rushed to keep him from dying from a life-threatening emergency. Moton is a Carolina Panthers offensive lineman. Except, he hasn't been an offensive lineman since the offseason because he was exclusively a patient trying to overcome the condition that caused, as he put it, "a multitude of clots in my right lung." DEION SANDERS DECLARES HE'S CANCER-FREE, ADDRESSES INCONTINENCE AHEAD OF COLORADO FOOTBALL SEASON People die from runaway blood clots. I had a friend die from blood clots in 2022. Miami Dolphins senior vice president Jason Jenkins died from a bilateral pulmonary thromboembolism due to phlebothrombosis. He was in his office at the team's training facility when it happened. Jenkins had complained of the pain clots in his legs caused him for months before that. He talked about how he had to be careful when he flew because that could impact his condition. So when Moton was placed on the non-football injury list in July it caught my attention because there had been reports about it being tied to clots since June. And that was extremely worrisome. But this column isn't all about sadness and concern. Or death. HOUSTON TEXANS STAR PRACTICES IN PADS FOR FIRST TIME IN NEARLY TWO YEARS AFTER 2024 CAREER-THREATENING INJURY That's because Moton is back on the Panthers practice field this week. And he was in the locker room on Tuesday talking about his victory over a life-threatening condition. "I was just hanging out about to take a nap, lay down, and all of sudden it started to feel like my chest was really congested," Moton told a group of reporters gathered at his locker. "I thought it was just normal chest congestion. But I started to taste blood in my mouth and then I knew something was up." One can only imagine what a world-class athlete who hadn't yet reached his 32nd birthday thinks when confronted with a serious medical emergency. These guys train to feel invincible. But Moton immediately realized he wasn't invincible. He was in deep trouble. "I started coughing up blood -- and it was like a lot of it," Moton said. "And I could start feeling it leaking through my chest even -- something like really different. So, after 15-or-something minutes, I was like 'Yeah, I've got to go to the hospital.' "Went to the hospital, they were doing CT scans, ultrasounds, trying to find what was going on. And that's when they found a multitude of clots in my right lung." Stunning. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! Moton said doctors to this day have not figured out what caused the frightening episode. "They put me on blood thinners, and other than that I was just working," he said. "I just couldn't have contact on the blood thinners because having contact on blood thinners can lead to like a brain bleed." Moton has been trying to stay in shape but it clearly isn't football shape. So he has 21 days to try to reach that kind of physical conditioning before a decision on his season's availability has to be made. The Panthers, dealing with injuries on their offensive line, need him as soon as possible. The man they're getting back has a different outlook than the one who last played a game in the 2025 season. "When you see the blood, you start thinking the worst," Moton said. "But thank God I'm still on this side of Earth, right? Like past football, man, it makes you count your blessings to be here. Still get to see my family. It's a blessing." And this: "Honestly," Moton added, "it gave me more gratitude for life in general." FOLLOW ARMANDO SALGUERO ON X: @ARMANDOSALGUERO

articles.title: Michael Penix Jr likely starting for Falcons against Bears despite rib injury, Kevin Stefanski says
articles.summary: Michael Penix Jr. left Sunday's game with a rib injury and was replaced by Tua Tagovailoa in overtime, but he's set to start against Chicago.
articles.body: The quarterback situation in Atlanta has been one of the NFL’s most closely watched storylines. After an offseason marked by injuries and a two-week stint with Cooper Rush under center, Atlanta appeared to find some stability when Michael Penix Jr. returned to the starting lineup. Late in Sunday’s hard-fought game against the Baltimore Ravens, Penix sustained a rib injury on a sack. He briefly returned before the end of regulation but could not continue in overtime, forcing Tua Tagovailoa to take over. Tagovailoa threw the game-ending interception, leaving Penix’s status for a pivotal Week 6 meeting with the Chicago Bears uncertain. After Penix underwent an MRI earlier this week, Falcons coach Kevin Stefanski said Wednesday that the quarterback is on track to start Sunday’s game, barring any setbacks. Penix was back at practice Wednesday, although he was listed as a limited participant. BACKUP QUARTERBACK TYLER HUNTLEY LEADS BALTIMORE RAVENS TO IMPROBABLE OT WIN OVER ATLANTA FALCONS Stefanski stopped short of offering details about what he knew about the extent of Penix's rib injury, instead telling reporters that the left-handed thrower is "feeling better." On Monday, ESPN’s Adam Schefter told "The Pat McAfee Show" that Penix’s rib injury "didn’t look like it’s a long-term injury" at the time. Penix’s practice workload this week will depend on how he feels, Stefanski said. "I want to see how he's feeling," Stefanski said. "With any injury like this, you want to make sure as they move around and how they're feeling -- it could be all, some, none. We shall see." ESPN reported later on Wednesday that Penix "took all the first-team reps in practice." "I felt good today at practice," Penix told reporters when asked the status of his ribs. "… I just gotta stay on top of my rehab and just make sure I'm doing all the right things." He added: "I feel good to go this week, so that's the plan." Penix’s injury history, dating back to his college days, is well documented. He suffered his latest ACL injury last November and underwent surgery. His recovery kept him out of the Falcons’ first two games this season. articles.title: 4 Arrested in the Shooting of San Francisco 49ers Player Keion White at a Super Bowl Party
articles.summary: SAN FRANCISCO (AP) — Four men have been arrested in connection with the shooting of San Francisco 49ers defensive lineman Keion White at a nightclub in February, officials said Wednesday.
articles.body:
SAN FRANCISCO (AP) — Four men have been arrested in connection with the shooting of San Francisco 49ers defensive lineman Keion White at a nightclub in February, officials said Wednesday.

The shooting occurred just after 4 a.m. on Feb. 9 at the crowded Mission District nightclub Dahlia, where White was hosting a private Super Bowl party.

White was shot in the ankle and taken to a local hospital for surgery, his team said at the time.

San Francisco Police Chief Derrick Lew said authorities arrested four men over the past week with the help of law enforcement agencies in Atlanta; Stockton, California; Irvine, California and Los Angeles.

The night of the shooting, multiple suspects with firearms "confronted" White, Lew said. Investigators used video footage and witness accounts to identify the men they say are the perpetrators.

On Oct. 7, local law enforcement arrested 35-year-old Curtis Green in Irvine, and two days later authorities arrested 36-year-old Gregory Walker of Mountain House, California, for their alleged involvement in the shooting.

The men were booked into San Francisco County Jail on Monday and scheduled to appear in court Wednesday afternoon. District Attorney Brooke Jenkins said prosecutors would seek no bail for Walker due to the public safety risk they said he poses. He will be charged with assault with a semiautomatic firearm — which prosecutors say he fired — as well as other charges for having a gun as a felon.

Green faces misdemeanor charges of brandishing a firearm and carrying a concealed and loaded gun in public, Jenkins said.

A message was left Wednesday with the San Francisco public defender's office to determine if its attorneys were representing the two men.

Two other men arrested in other jurisdictions are not yet in local custody and will be charged once they are brought to San Francisco, Jenkins said.

One of the other men expected to face charges in San Francisco was arrested Oct. 7 in Atlanta. The 38-year-old was arrested on a no-bail warrant. Authorities say police seized an illegal firearm during the arrest, along with thousands of grams of MDMA, methamphetamine, cocaine and fentanyl at the man's home.

That same day, law enforcement arrested a 36-year-old man in Stockton, California, in connection with White's shooting, and recovered a loaded firearm, over 100 oxycodone pills and $7,000 in cash.

articles.title: Broncos lose star player 24 hours before Thursday Night Football Week 6
articles.summary: Broncos get bad news before TNF against Seahawks.
articles.body:
The Denver Broncos just suffered a massive blow less than 24 hours before Thursday Night Football . The Broncos will be without star cornerback Pat Surtain II when they host the Seattle Seahawks in Week 6, leaving Denver without one of the best defensive backs in the NFL for a matchup against an explosive Seattle passing attack.

Pat Surtain II (ankle) listed out for Week 6. — Underdog NFL (@UnderdogNFL) October 14, 2026

Pat Surtain II (ankle) listed out for Week 6.

Underdog NFL (@UnderdogNFL) October 14, 2026

Surtain was officially ruled out Wednesday with an ankle injury after missing practice throughout the week. The timing could hardly be worse for Denver. The Broncos are preparing to face Jaxon Smith-Njigba, who currently leads the NFL in receiving yards with 583 through five games.

Pat Surtain's absence is a massive problem

Jan 4, 2026; Denver, Colorado, USA; Denver Broncos cornerback Pat Surtain II (2) reacts with safety Devon Key (26) after a play in the fourth quarter against the Los Angeles Chargers at Empower Field at Mile High. Mandatory Credit: Isaiah J. Downing-Imagn Images

Surtain isn't just another starting cornerback. The former NFL Defensive Player of the Year is the centerpiece of Denver's secondary and allows defensive coordinator Vance Joseph to build his game plans around having a premier corner capable of limiting an opponent's top receiving threat.

Now, Denver will have to find a different way to defend Seattle's most dangerous offensive weapon.

Smith-Njigba has been one of the NFL's most productive receivers this season, and his production has continued even while dealing with an ankle issue. He was listed as a limited participant for the second consecutive day Tuesday, but he finished Seattle's Week 5 loss to San Francisco with five catches for 102 yards and a touchdown.

Broncos secondary takes another major hit

Nov 30, 2025; Landover, Maryland, USA; Denver Broncos cornerback Pat Surtain II (2) tackles Washington Commanders tight end Zach Ertz (86) in the first quarter of the game at Northwest Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Peter Casey-Imagn Images

The Surtain news is even more concerning because Denver won't have its full complement of defensive backs. Safety Talanoa Hufanga has also been ruled out and is expected to miss multiple weeks with an ankle injury.

Cornerback Riley Moss is listed as questionable after missing last week's game with a rib injury, although he has returned to limited participation this week.

That leaves Denver potentially facing Seattle without two of its most important defensive backs while trying to slow down Smith-Njigba and an offense that has shown the ability to create explosive plays through the air.

The Broncos managed to beat the Chargers last week despite Surtain's absence, but Seattle presents a very different challenge. Smith-Njigba is playing at an elite level, and losing Surtain removes Denver's best option for making life difficult for the Seahawks' star receiver.

articles.title: Bengals rank near NFL's bottom in play-action usage through Week 5
articles.summary: The Bengals are using play action on just 12.2% of their offensive snaps this season, the second-lowest rate in the NFL.
articles.body:
The Cincinnati Bengals have a supremely talented NFL passing attack, but they are an outlier in how rarely they use play action.

Per Sharp Football Analysis , Cincinnati has used play action on just 12.2% of its offensive snaps this season. That ranks 31st among 32 teams, ahead of only the Philadelphia Eagles at 10.4%.

The New Orleans Saints are next at 12.3%, while no other team sits below 12.9%.

It continues a trend from last season. Pro Football Focus noted that Cincinnati used play action at a 17.1% rate in 2025, well below the NFL average of 25.65%.

Despite that tendency, Joe Burrow and the Bengals offense have produced. Cincinnati comes into its Week 6 bye at 3-2 while averaging 25.6 points per game. Burrow threw four touchdown passes in a 31-24 win over the Miami Dolphins in Week 5.

Regardless, the play-action number is an evident offensive tendency to evaluate during the bye before an AFC North matchup with the Baltimore Ravens in Week 7.

articles.title: Cardinals HC Mike LaFleur seems to be in dire straits in the desert
articles.summary: Arizona Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur has not delivered the dynamic turnaround, but he must assume responsibility for recent let downs.
articles.body:
The underwhelming statistical output the Arizona Cardinals have yielded for throughout the first five games of the NFL season has been quite dismal. Furthermore, fans and critics may begin to contemplate whether team administration made the right decision by hiring first-year head coach Mike LaFleur.

LaFleur wasn't the primary choice nor too candidate but was a secondary option after the Las Vegas Raiders hired Klint Kubiak as their head coach earlier this year. LaFleur's repertoire didn't have a hefty acclaim but his connection and operative role as an assistant to Los Angeles Rams head coach Sean McVay did summon him some favor. LaFleur also spent a few years with the New York Jets and other franchises as well. Still, operating as a head coach in the NFL takes a certain leadership quality that has not really been exemplified by LaFleur in the first five games. A combination of team turnovers, lack of discipline, penalties and utter offensive indecision in strategy all seem to mirror the novice disposition of LaFleur who quite frankly has not showed himself to be competent so far.

Many Cardinals' fans question whether or not defensive coordinator Nick Rallis should've been retained but an analytical deeper look shows that the Arizona Cardinals offense has been quite counterproductive. Thus without an ability to sustain offensive drives, A area facet that the newly head coach was supposed to edify, It's very difficult not to share some spotlight on LaFleur and his shortcomings.
